title: Audit inherited planning-node dependencies for deadlock
description:
Scaffolding the planning bracket moves a container's pre-existing upstream dependencies onto the planning node. A moved dependency that cannot complete before the plan is authored deadlocks the bracket: the planning node can never close, so breakdown never releases. The planning workflow needs an explicit audit-and-re-home procedure for these inherited edges.

## Background

Observed on the f2532a2d bracket (2026-07-02): the planning node inherited a dependency on an in-progress external task whose real consumer was one future implementation child, not the plan authoring itself. The session resolved it ad hoc by re-homing the edge onto the consuming child at breakdown time and recording the move as a plan decision, which both the plan reviewer and the gate accepted. The pattern is general: the move-upstream transform is semantically right for dependencies the planning genuinely needs, and wrong for dependencies only the implementation consumes.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The jit-planning-lead workflow instructs auditing the planning node's inherited upstream dependencies before plan completion, classifying each as planning-required or implementation-consumed.
- [hard] REQ-02: For an implementation-consumed dependency, the documented procedure re-homes the edge onto the consuming child at breakdown time and records the move with its rationale in the plan's decision log.
- [hard] REQ-03: For a planning-required dependency that cannot complete, the documented procedure is to escalate to the requester rather than drop the edge or force the plan through.
